sources.title: Pod Priority and Preemption
sources.supports: Kubernetes documents numeric pod priority and scheduler preemption of lower-priority pods. Used only to distinguish ordering priority from eligibility and to identify preemption as a poor fit for leased agent work.

sources.title: API Priority and Fairness
sources.supports: Kubernetes API server request classification, priority levels, queues and fair dispatch as concurrency sharing. Supports separating priority from fairness; not a backlog-selection algorithm.

sources.title: Workflow message passing
sources.supports: Temporal documents Query/Signal/Update distinction, validation, accepted/completed status, update IDs and asynchronous message processing. Used as a workflow-control-plane precedent, not a Fleet dependency recommendation.

sources.title: Events and Event History
sources.supports: Temporal describes an append-only durable event history used for recovery/replay, plus explicit history limits and principal attribution. Supports replay and provenance tradeoff discussion.

sources.title: CloudEvents Specification v1.0.2
sources.supports: CloudEvents defines an interoperable event envelope with required source/id/specversion/type, duplicate identity semantics for source+id, optional time/subject/dataschema, and compact payload guidance. It does not define queue ordering or Fleet field authority.

sources.title: Introduction — Apache Kafka 4.4
sources.access: Located using official Apache Kafka search result; official page states same-key events use one partition and consumers read partition events in write order
sources.supports: Kafka documents per-partition order for same-key events. Used to bound the claim: this does not provide global total order across keys or external projections.

sources.title: Isolation In SQLite
sources.supports: SQLite documents serializable transactions implemented by serialized writes, one writer at a time, and WAL snapshot behavior. Used as storage-family concurrency context only.

sources.title: Embedded Replicas
sources.access: Fetched successfully with webfetch after obsolete /sync/embedded-replicas path returned 404
sources.supports: The page says Embedded Replica reads are served locally; writes by default go to the remote primary, then the initiating replica is updated (read-your-writes); other replicas see changes on sync/periodic sync. It distinguishes Turso Sync as local-first with explicit push/pull. Does not establish which mode this repository runs.

sources.title: Best practices for using webhooks
sources.supports: GitHub recommends webhook secrets/HTTPS, responding 2xx within 10 seconds, async processing for longer work, redelivery, and X-GitHub-Delivery deduplication; redelivery reuses delivery ID.

sources.title: Using the API to manage Projects / GitHub GraphQL Projects reference
sources.access: Found by official GitHub Docs web search
sources.supports: GitHub documents Project item field reads/updates; GraphQL Projects reference documents POSITION ordering for project items. Used to establish API/projection surface, not portable canonical queue order or transaction semantics.

sources.title: Project priority
sources.supports: Linear documents optional project priority categories and manual/micro-adjusted position within a shared priority group. Used as UX prior art for separate category and local within-group order.

sources.title: Rank an issue / Enable ranking; LexoRank system troubleshooting
sources.access: Official Jira page fetched; navigation-heavy response, and official search result confirms manual ranking and ranking configuration
sources.supports: Jira supports manual work-item ranking; official Atlassian LexoRank support material discusses rebalance and rank-system maintenance. Used to make rebalance an explicit design cost, not to claim a DIY rank implementation is safe.

sources.title: Troubleshooting LexoRank System Issues
sources.access: Found by official Atlassian search result
sources.supports: Atlassian support notes cluster-safe rank operations and rank-length thresholds/rebalance behavior for named Jira versions. Illustrates rank maintenance costs; exact thresholds are product-specific and not generalized.
